audit: Data-integrity problems: 63 mutation rows are internally impossible - protein positions far beyond the protein length (e.g. BCOR p.P101537F, NOTCH2 p.E127469G, NF2 p.P21404E; BCOR is ~1755 aa, NOTCH2 ~2471, NF2 ~595) or missense changes not reachable by any single-nucleotide substitution. They are concentrated in exactly four gene-diagnosis pairs that would otherwise rank among the top hits: NOTCH2 in embryonal RMS (19/75), MED12 in ependymoma (15/81), BCOR in medulloblastoma, and NF2 in pilocytic astrocytoma. These look like injected/corrupted records; I removed them and did not claim those pairs (MED12-ependymoma retains a few plausible-looking rows but comes from the same contaminated set, so I do not trust it). BCOR in SHH medulloblastoma is real biology, but the genuine signal here is ~1 case. Other concerns: 10 hypermutated tumours (500-15,700 mutations; mostly gliomas, likely MMR/POLE) were excluded as they inflate gene-level counts; recurrent identical variants across unrelated diagnoses (C17orf80 p.S281R in 72 cases, HLTF p.Q898E, ZNF510, CD69, CD46, ABCF1 p.P9L) look like germline leakage or calling artefacts; several cases have identical single-mutation profiles (e.g. 9 cases with only BRAF p.V640E, the V600E equivalent in an alternative transcript) - plausible for LGG but possible duplicates. Diagnosis labels are heterogeneous and overlapping (Glioma, malignant vs glioblastoma vs astrocytoma; RMS NOS vs embryonal RMS; 'missing', 'Unknown' and 'Neoplasm, NOS' categories), so 'rest of cohort' comparisons are diluted by related tumours. WES SNV/indel data miss fusions and CNVs (e.g. KIAA1549-BRAF in pilocytic astrocytoma, PAX-FOXO1), so frequencies are for point mutations only. Many diagnoses have <15 cases, so frequencies there are imprecise.
methods: Python stdlib only. Joined cases and mutations; flagged and removed impossible protein changes (position exceeding protein length for affected genes, or missense not reachable by a single-base change); excluded 10 hypermutated cases (>300 mutations). For every diagnosis x gene, counted cases with >=1 non-synonymous mutation and ran a one-sided Fisher exact (hypergeometric) test versus all other cases, ranking by p-value with Bonferroni/BH perspective (~5e5 tests). Retained hits that are strongly significant or moderately significant with a known driver/hotspot pattern (inspected variant positions), and discarded passenger-like large genes and recurrent artefact variants. Expected frequency is the observed fraction lightly shrunk for small groups; probability reflects significance, sample size and prior biology.
